source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Analogical prompting: one prompt tells the model to recall relevant problems with solutions, then solve the target. It beats 0-shot CoT and fixed few-shot CoT on math and code.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo: 0-shot 75.0, 0-shot CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated exemplars 77.8. MATH GPT-3.5: 33.0/33.9/34.9/37.3. PaLM2 GSM8K 60.8/78.2/80.7/81.7. K=5 exemplars for GSM8K, K=3 for MATH and BIG-Bench.
limits: Table columns read from garbled PDF layout; gain over fixed 5-shot CoT on GSM8K with GPT-3.5 is only 1.1 points. c04 shows relevance is not the cause.
agent_relevance: The model does its own 'access' step in one pass. Cheap and needs no library, but the gain may not come from analogy.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Adding self-generated high-level knowledge (a tutorial) before exemplars helps on hard code tasks, because low-level exemplars alone make the model copy specifics.
numbers: Codeforces Acc@1 GPT-3.5-turbo-16k: 0-shot 8%, 0-shot CoT 9%, 3-shot CoT 11%, self-generated exemplars 13%, knowledge then exemplars 15%. GPT-4: 16/16/17/17/19%. Knowledge-before-exemplars beat the reverse order (Table 7 ablation).
limits: Small absolute numbers; Acc@10 gains are mixed.
agent_relevance: Retrieval cue should carry abstract concepts first, then cases. Supports an abstract-encoding step before access.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Self-generation depends on model scale. Weak models cannot produce valid exemplars; for them retrieval from a labelled bank is better. For strong models self-generation wins over embedding retrieval.
numbers: GSM8K across model strengths (Table 4): strongest column about 61% self-generated vs 54% for 5-shot retrieved (Sentence-BERT cosine, top-5 from the training set) vs 50% fixed 5-shot vs 14% 0-shot CoT. For the weakest models (curie, davinci-001) retrieved CoT was better.
limits: Table cells partly garbled in text extraction; direction is stated in the paper text. Retrieved exemplars are guaranteed correct, generated ones are not.
agent_relevance: Use generated analogues only with a strong model; with a weak one, retrieve verified cases.

source: Relevant or Random: Can LLMs Truly Perform Analogical Reasoning? (2024)
finding: Self-generated exemplars that are relevant did no better than random ones. Correctness of the self-generated examples matters more than relevance.
numbers: GPT-3.5, GSM8K 500 items x 3 seeds: relevant 71.5, no-exemplar 75.5, random same-domain 75.1, random different-domain 76.3, random biology 75.3. MATH: relevant 33.3, none 36.1, random 34.1-36.3. Manual check on MATH: exemplar correct 62% (relevant) vs 86% (random same). Cosine relevance: relevant 0.54, random bio 0.06.
quote: Random biological examples score 3.8 points above relevant ones on GSM8K
limits: Mainly GPT-3.5; checks on GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3 and Qwen2.5 agree in direction.
agent_relevance: Key warning: the 'access' effect in LLMs may be a format or priming effect, not analogy. Do not credit retrieval of a case unless a held-out test shows it.

source: Relevant or Random: Can LLMs Truly Perform Analogical Reasoning? (2024)
finding: A fixed, hand-checked set of generated problems reused for every query beats per-query self-generated relevant exemplars and is cheaper.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5: fixed math set 75.7, fixed biology set 77.9 vs relevant 71.5 (+6.4). Llama-3.1-8B: 81.0 vs 74.8. Qwen2.5-14B: 91.1 vs 86.5. Wrong answers in the demos cost about 5 points (56.3 vs 50.9 average). Repeating one problem scored 55.0 vs 56.3 for diverse ones.
limits: Fixed sets are task-type specific; diversity helps modestly.
agent_relevance: Supports guardrail G3 style checking: a verified small library beats fresh unverified recall. Diversity among cases matters.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 reproduced the Gick and Holyoak pattern qualitatively. Alone, the radiation problem gets a non-analogical answer (inject a source into the tumour). After the convergence story it finds the convergence solution. With two distractor stories it fails again until prompted to consider the earlier stories.
numbers: Qualitative single-case tests (supplement S5.1-S5.5). Story analogies (Gentner materials, N=54 students): both GPT-3 and humans prefer the target sharing causal relations (GPT-3 binomial p=0.0005); students beat GPT-3 on this task (OR=0.37, p=0.0003); GPT-4 near-perfect in the near condition.
quote: GPT-3 no longer identified the convergence solution
limits: No trial counts for the radiation test; the radiation story is likely in training data (authors say GPT-3 knows it). The prompt hint ('one of the stories you read before will give you a hint') is what rescued access.
agent_relevance: A hint line that says 'one earlier case may help' converted failed access into success. A cheap trigger for the retrieval step.

source: Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in large language models (2024)
finding: On counterfactual letter-string problems (altered alphabets, unlikely in training data) models fall well below humans, while humans stay steady.
numbers: Overall letter-string accuracy: humans 0.753 (134 kept of 136 recruited, 14 problems each), GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452.
limits: Only letter strings in the opened version; per-condition numbers are in figures only; Webb et al. 2024 reply argues task demands explain part of the gap.
agent_relevance: Analogy skill in models may rest on familiar surface forms. Test our agent on counterfactual re-skins of cases.

source: Musker, Duchnowski, Millière, Pavlick (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning
finding: Best LLMs match humans on analogies that need re-representation, but react differently to controls: they are sensitive to order and to irrelevant semantic distractors.
numbers: Semantic-content study: humans and Claude 3 Opus about 0.70 match to reference; GPT-4 and Llama-405B about 0.35. Permuted presentation order drops LLMs, not humans. Small prompt changes moved GPT-4 from about 20% to about 100% (Only RHS) and from near 0 to about 40% (Random Finals).
limits: Match-to-reference grading; best models only; reasoning models left to future work.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording alone can swing results by 60-80 points, so any retrieval-by-analogy step needs several prompt variants tested.

source: ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives (2024)
finding: Models pick the right analogy among distractors well when it is near (same domain) but poorly when it is far. Surface-sharing distractors hurt most, especially shared actions.
numbers: 1,096 triples. Humans 96.0% overall (far 94.1%). Zero-shot GPT-4: near analogy with far distractor 94.0, far analogy with far distractor 57.1, far analogy with near (surface) distractor 29.1 (random 50). GPT-3.5: 50.4 and 21.7. SBERT: 12.6 and 1.0 on far items. Chain-of-thought lifted GPT models by up to about 30 points on far analogies; few-shot gave about 10 points to GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 on far items but cost near-item accuracy.
quote: Distractors that share surface mappings with the query are harder for most models
limits: Multiple-choice choosing, not open retrieval; 120 items in the human study.
agent_relevance: This is the MAC/FAC surface bias reproduced in models: a surface-matching distractor drives them below chance. Embeddings alone (SBERT) are worst. CoT is the lever that helped.

source: StoryAnalogy: Deriving Story-level Analogies from Large Language Models (2023)
finding: Models chose the most analogous story poorly; hard negatives (similar entities) lured them, which looks like surface similarity. A structure-aware matcher did better than prompted LLMs.
numbers: 24K story pairs. Multiple choice (random 25%): humans 85.7%, text-davinci-003 averaged 37.1%, best LLM 37.7 points below humans. The structure baseline of Sultan and Shahaf (entity-cluster mapping) scored 44.9% and resisted hard negatives. More demonstrations gave no consistent gain; fine-tuning on the corpus helped.
limits: Stories are mostly LLM-generated then human-rated.
agent_relevance: A structural matcher beat prompted LLMs at choosing among surface-matched candidates, which supports a separate code-side structural stage.

source: Czinczoll et al. (2022) Scientific and Creative Analogies in Pretrained Language Models (SCAN)
finding: Pretrained models (GloVe, BERT, GPT-2) do worse on cross-domain analogies than on same-domain word analogies; one worked example in the prompt mostly did not help.
numbers: SCAN: 449 analogy instances in 65 concept mappings (for example war to argument, virus to malware). MRR lower on SCAN than BATS for all models; one-shot prompting did not help except GPT-2 on BATS.
limits: Old models; I read setup and discussion, not every table cell.
agent_relevance: Background: distance between domains drives failure, as in humans.

source: Can LLMs Help Improve Analogical Reasoning For Strategic Decisions? Experimental Evidence from Humans and GPT-4 (2025)
finding: A direct Gick and Holyoak design with business problems, 199 students and 60 GPT-4 runs. Without a hint GPT-4 almost never used the source story; with a hint it used it every time, but also used wrong analogies.
numbers: Humans without/with hint: factory problem 6.3% / 8.7% (4/46); HR problem 20.3% / 37% (17/46); original G&H 1983 was 29% / 50% (8/28, 14/28). GPT-4 no hint: radiation analogy used in 1/15 runs, dolphin story 14/15. With hint: recall 1.00, precision 0.50-0.52, accuracy 0.50-0.53; humans precision 0.67-0.75, recall 0.26-0.39, accuracy 0.57-0.63.
quote: GPT-4 achieves high recall but suffers from low precision
limits: Preprint; two-source matching is harder than the original one-source task; GPT-4 may know the radiation story from training; my reading of which problem maps to which story is uncertain.
agent_relevance: GPT-4 is an eager retriever with low precision: its failures come from surface features. A hint raises recall, so the check must be in code: require a stated mapping and a held-out test before an analogue is used.

source: Can LLMs Help Improve Analogical Reasoning For Strategic Decisions? (2025)
finding: False analogies by GPT-4 were mostly surface-driven, by humans mostly wrong causal schemas. GPT-4 also used both source stories when both were offered (demand effect).
numbers: Mis-transfers coded surface vs structural by Holyoak and Koh definitions; GPT-4 mostly surface or 'both', humans mostly structural (from a figure, no exact counts).
limits: Counts only in figures.
agent_relevance: Do not offer a model several cases and demand use; it will force all of them. Offer one at a time with a fit test.

source: Forbus, Gentner, Law (1995) MAC/FAC: A model of similarity-based retrieval
finding: The cheap first stage (dot product of content vectors) plus an expensive structural second stage (SME) reproduces the human retrievability order literal similarity > surface > analogy > relational-only.
numbers: Karla-the-hawk stories, 9 story sets (45 stories). Human reminding rates: LS .56, SF .53, AN .12, FOR .09. Sim 2 (36 stories in memory): MAC passes LS .78, SF .67, AN .33, FOR .22; FAC keeps .78/.44/.11/0. Sim 3 (no LS in memory): SF .89 MAC / .78 FAC, AN .56 / .45. Rival ARCS had two order violations.
limits: Hand-encoded predicate representations; small memory (18-36 items vs 32 stories plus life memory for people).
agent_relevance: Direct blueprint: fast cheap candidate sweep, then structural filter in code. An LLM embedding plays the MAC stage; the FAC stage needs structural comparison, which prompts do poorly (c09, c10).

source: Forbus, Gentner, Law (1995) MAC/FAC
finding: FAC rejects most surface-only matches that MAC lets through, and keeps partial structural matches when no perfect match exists. Selection rule: best match plus any within 10%.
numbers: MAC retrieves 3.3 items on average, FAC accepts 1.5.
limits: Parameter 10% chosen from pilot studies.
agent_relevance: Keep the selector in code with a margin rule, and let 'nothing reminded' be a valid outcome.

source: Accelerating Innovation Through Analogy Mining (2017)
finding: Older retrieval system: crowd-labelled purpose and mechanism parts of product texts, vectors learned with an RNN, then retrieval of 'same purpose, different mechanism' products. Retrieved items raised the share of good ideas.
numbers: About 5,500 training and 2,500 test products. Ideation study with 38 AMT workers, 12 seed products, 749 ideas: probability an idea is good 0.71 [0.48, 0.87] for the method vs 0.28 [0.16, 0.44] for TF-IDF and 0.27 [0.16, 0.41] for random (k=2 majority vote). A scaffolded crowd task (concrete, then abstract schema) reduced surface-only labels.
limits: Crowd and product domain; inspiration shown after one minute of unaided ideas.
agent_relevance: Shows access by an abstracted representation (purpose and mechanism) works downstream. An LLM can write purpose and mechanism fields; the study design is copyable.

source: Learning by Analogy: Enhancing Few-Shot Prompting for Math Word Problem Solving with Computational Graph-Based Retrieval (2024)
finding: Retrieving exemplars by matching the problem's computational graph (structure) beats retrieving by BGE text embedding, most for small models.
numbers: 6 datasets, top-8 exemplars. Average exact match, random / BGE / graph: 0.5B 18.6/27.6/34.3 (+6.7 over BGE); 1B 27.6/40.7/47.1; 3B 52.7/57.6/60.8; 8B 59.7/66.2/68.8; 70B 66.3/72.8/74.4 (+1.6). Math23k +14.5 over BGE at 0.5B; math_qa -0.7 (semantic and graph similarity overlap there). Upper bound with true graphs 68.2 vs 66.6 achieved on Math23k.
quote: semantic retrieval tends to prioritize superficial linguistic similarity over deep structural alignment
limits: Graphs were given annotations for one dataset; retriever trained on a quarter of it; gain shrinks as the generator grows.
agent_relevance: Cleanest controlled evidence that structural keys beat semantic embeddings for retrieving solved problems, and that the benefit is largest when the solver is weak.

source: MetaLadder: Ascending Mathematical Solution Quality via Analogical-Problem Reasoning Transfer (2025)
finding: Training the model to recall an analogous solved problem, restate the problem, then solve gives gains over CoT; the restating step matters more than the analogy step.
numbers: LLaMA3-8B average over 6 sets: CoT 36.1, MetaLadder 39.4, best variant 42.8; GSM8K 61.5 to 66.2. DeepSeekMath-7B: CoT 47.3 to 52.1 (best 57.6), GSM8K 64.2 to 69.4. Ablation (LLaMA, avg): full 44.3, w/o restate 41.8, w/o analogy 42.9, w/o strategy 43.6. Skipping the analogy step at inference raised scores by 1.6-1.8 and saved time (1343 s vs 2181 s on MATH).
limits: Fine-tuned models, not a pure scaffold; analogues are generated, not retrieved; two 7-8B models only.
agent_relevance: Restating the problem in abstract terms (abstract encoding) is worth more than recalling a case. Another sign that 'recall a case' is the weak part.

source: MetaLadder (2025) self-evolve variant
finding: Self-evolve: the model's own correct analogous problems become new training data.
numbers: LLaMA adds about 7K samples (15K to 22K), +1.5 points; DeepSeek +0.5.
limits: Training-time; not usable in a no-training scaffold.
agent_relevance: Low relevance for a no-training scaffold; keep as a pointer.

source: Thought Propagation: An Analogical Approach to Complex Reasoning with Large Language Models (2024)
finding: The agent proposes analogous problems, solves them, and aggregates their results to refine its own answer or to build a plan. Plug-and-play over IO and CoT prompting.
numbers: Shortest-path (100 generated graphs) +12% optimal paths; creative writing (100 prompts) +13% human preference; ALFWorld (134 environments) +15% task completion. Tree-of-Thought scored below plain IO on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 for shortest path. 2-layer TP gave small gains over 1-layer at higher token cost; 5-shot gave little over 1-shot.
limits: Average figures taken from the abstract; I read the table text only partly; analogues are generated by the same model so they share its blind spots (G4).
agent_relevance: A method from this subfield inside an agent loop: generate neighbours, solve, aggregate. Needs a code-side check on aggregation.

source: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (2024)
finding: An agent that retrieves similar successful trajectories by task similarity and also keeps abstracted insights improves over ReAct. Retrieval and insights are complementary.
numbers: HotpotQA: ReAct 28.0, ExpeL 39.0. ALFWorld: ReAct 40.0, ExpeL 59.0. WebShop reward 0.666 vs 0.701. Ablation insights-only / retrieval-only: HotpotQA 36/31, ALFWorld 50/55, WebShop 37/38. HotpotQA to FEVER transfer: ReAct 63, ExpeL 70.
limits: Retrieval is by task-text similarity (surface); no structure-based test; the paper text and table disagree on one ALFWorld number.
agent_relevance: A real example of access inside an agent loop; shows case retrieval and abstract rules add together.

source: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (2025)
finding: Case-based memory (write each finished case, read top-K by cosine similarity of state encodings) lifts a deep research agent, most out of distribution; K=4 is enough.
numbers: Average over 7 QA sets: no CBR 59.9 F1 / 72.2 PM, with CBR 66.6 / 80.4. Out-of-distribution sets (MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA) +4.7 to +9.6 points. K=0: 59.9 F1; K=4: 64.5 (best); K=32: 63.9. GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%. Learned retriever slightly beat non-parametric: 85.44 vs 84.85 after five rounds.
limits: Embedding-similarity retrieval; learned-retriever gain is small; no surface-versus-structure ablation.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a case library works at small K and that more cases hurt. Matches c01: few cases suffice.

source: Beyond Experience Retrieval: Learning to Generate Utility-Optimized Structured Experience for Frozen LLMs (SEAM) (2026)
finding: The authors argue that experience retrieval is optimised for surface similarity rather than usefulness to the solver, so similar entries can miss key checks or add noise.
numbers: Claim read in the paper's introduction; SEAM is trained with GRPO to write a structured experience entry; gains on four maths benchmarks, larger on harder ones. I did not extract per-benchmark numbers.
limits: Needs training of a small module, not our setting.
agent_relevance: Supports scoring retrieved cases by measured utility on our own runs instead of text similarity.

source: Reason Analogically via Cross-domain Prior Knowledge: An Empirical Study of Cross-domain Knowledge Transfer for In-Context Learning (2026)
finding: Demonstrations retrieved from a different domain can help a target domain, but only for models above a size threshold. Gains come from repaired reasoning structure, not semantic cues.
numbers: 25 transfer directions, 6 reasoning benchmarks (including ProofWriter, ProntoQA, FOLIO, LogicalDeduction, GSM8K, AR-LSAT); Qwen2.5 3B-32B, Gemma-3, Llama-3, Qwen3. Embedding retrieval (bge-large-en-v1.5) improved accuracy by +12.3% for ProofWriter to LogicalDeduction and +10.3% for ProntoQA to LogicalDeduction. Small models (3B-7B) show negative transfer and no gain from more shots; the 27B model gains with more demos. Repair ratios of earlier failures were 52-66% for the best query type but 18-37% for others.
limits: Exact match on benchmark tasks; transfer is conditional; the retrievers tested (embedding, BM25) are not structure-aware.
agent_relevance: Cross-domain access works when the case carries a reasoning pattern, and the diversity of reasoning structures in retrieved cases matters. Gate use on model strength.

source: Teaching Through Analogies: A Modular Pipeline for Educational Analogy Generation (2026)
finding: Adding structural sub-concepts (the parts that map) to the query improves embedding retrieval of the right source system; LLM re-ranking gives the best top-1 pick, embeddings the best top-2 and top-3.
numbers: 7 embedding models, 12 LLMs, SCAR (400 instances) and ParallelPARC. SCAR retrieval: OpenAI-large 0.710 to 0.792 with sub-concepts, OpenAI-small 0.677 to 0.780, average 0.557 to 0.673. Re-ranking Hit@1: gold sub-concepts 24.5%, background 22.2%, embedding-only 19.5%, generated sub-concepts 18.2%, names only 17.5%; Hit@2/3 embedding-only 30.5%/40.0%. Open generation: sub-concepts add only 0.4-1.6 points; best Hit@20 75.4%.
limits: Stages scored separately, not end to end; the 0.7 similarity threshold is untested; gold annotations helped more than generated ones.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for a two-stage design: embeddings narrow, an LLM over explicit structure picks. Abstract encoding (sub-concepts) helps access.

source: BRIGHT: A Realistic and Challenging Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval (2024)
finding: Standard embedding retrievers fail when relevance needs reasoning rather than word overlap. Rewriting the query with explicit reasoning helps.
numbers: 1,384 queries. The leading MTEB model scored 59.0 nDCG@10 on MTEB but 18.3 on BRIGHT; reasoning-based query rewriting added up to 12.2 points.
limits: Abstract page only, so opened is false.
agent_relevance: Indirect support: retrieval keys must carry the abstract reasoning pattern, not the topic words.

source: Reliable Proof Generation with LLMs via Analogical Retrieval and Symbolic Verification: A Case Study in Euclidean Geometry (2025)
finding: Structure-based retrieval of analogous solved problems plus a symbolic verifier gives large gains in formal geometry proofs.
numbers: FormalGeo-7k, 50 test problems (10 per difficulty level). Keys: problems abstracted (names to <word>, numbers to <num>), Jaccard on constructions and on conditions, goal match; an MLP predicts proof similarity; top k=5 proofs as examples. One run, no retries, base to ours: o1 10 to 48, GPT-5 44 to 64, Gemini-2.5-Flash 22 to 48, Claude Sonnet 4.6 28 to 60. With retries: 38 to 68, 80 to 96, 58 to 74, 58 to 78. Ablation (Gemini / Claude): full 48/60, retrieved analogues with full theorem dictionary 30/42, random examples 24/28, baseline 22/28.
limits: Only geometry and 50 items; abstraction is simple; the Z3 verifier supplies the retries, so gain is shared between analogy and verifier.
agent_relevance: Closest match to our design: structural key, few analogues (k=5), and a code-run verifier independent of the model. Retrieval alone gave +8 to +14 points over random examples.

source: CHAIRO: Contextual Hierarchical Analogical Induction and Reasoning Optimization for LLMs (2026)
finding: Retrieving k-NN analogical examples (BGE-M3) to induce rules, then injecting the rules, beats static RAG in content moderation.
numbers: Qwen3-8B base. Overall F1 89.2 vs DeepSeek V3 80.3. Replacing k-NN retrieval with random selection lost 2.3 F1 (86.9). Explicit rules +5.3 F1 over plain SFT; analogical examples in rule induction +4.5 F1; end-to-end vs static RAG +2.3. Weaker on Pornography (71.5) and Gambling (82.0).
limits: Needs training; text moderation only.
agent_relevance: Retrieved cases are useful as raw material for a rule, not only as a demo; links to the schema induction subfield.

source: Search-level cross-check of agent-memory papers c21, c22, c23
finding: Across the agent-memory papers I opened (ExpeL, Memento, SEAM) retrieval is by embedding similarity, and none compares relational-structure retrieval against embedding retrieval inside the agent loop. The only structure-versus-embedding tests I found are on maths, geometry and analogy generation.
numbers: No agent-memory head-to-head numbers. Structure-vs-embedding comparisons: c17 (math, +1.6 to +6.7 exact match), c27 (geometry, +8 to +14 over random examples), c25 (sub-concepts, +0.08 to +0.10 retrieval score).
limits: Absence in the papers I opened, not a full search of agent memory work.
agent_relevance: Open gap: test structural versus embedding access in our own loop.

source: Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (2023)
finding: Reply to the counterfactual-task critique: argues task demands, not missing reasoning, cause part of the drop on altered tasks.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Title seen in search listing only; not opened.
agent_relevance: Do not over-read counterfactual failures as proof of no analogy ability; also do not accept success at face value.
